evidence.text: How do cosmological moduli change the post-inflationary history before BBN, and what follows for dark matter, baryogenesis, CMB inference and small-scale structure?

sources.title: Preheating After Modular Inflation

evidence.text: Estimate visible-sector decay rates by canonical normalization and diagonalization of mixed moduli, using gauge and fermion couplings and perturbative widths. Convert rates to reheat temperatures with Tr≈0.1√(ΓMP).

sources.title: Reheating for Closed String Inflation

evidence.text: Use running gauge couplings, gaugino condensation and the symmetry-constrained Affleck–Dine–Seiberg superpotential to analyse hidden SU(Nc) theories with Nf = 0 or 0 < Nf < Nc−1; include supersymmetry-breaking scalar masses when discussing their low-energy spectra.

sources.title: Inflation in string theory: A Graceful exit to the real world

evidence.text: Expands moduli about their vacuum values and diagonalises the kinetic/mass system to obtain canonical fields. Couplings are obtained by expanding the moduli-dependent kinetic and mass terms of open-string modes and expressing them in canonical variables. The paper imports the detailed coupling calculations from earlier work.

sources.title: Inflationary constraints on modulus dominated cosmology

evidence.text: Express the modulus-dominated duration using its lifetime, the equality Hubble scale and initial displacement; combine this with slow-roll relations and observational normalization. Reheating is parameterized by an effective equation of state and its duration rather than a detailed decay model.

sources.title: Cosmological Moduli and the Post-Inflationary Universe: A Critical Review

evidence.text: Boltzmann evolution for WIMPs, classical axion oscillator equations, and number-to-entropy yields organize production, annihilation and dilution during modulus domination and reheating.

sources.title: Trans-Planckian censorship conjecture and nonthermal post-inflationary history

evidence.text: For each beginning and end of moduli domination, numerically adjust the end of inflation until an initially Planck-length mode saturates TCC. A separate approximate geometrical argument uses radiation and matter slopes to interpret the limited enhancement.

sources.title: Confronting Kähler moduli inflation with CMB data

evidence.text: How do the model-dependent duration of post-inflationary modulus domination and uncertain reheating alter the pivot e-fold count, inferred microscopic parameters, and CMB compatibility of Kähler moduli inflation?

sources.title: Inflation in realistic D-brane models

evidence.text: Can D3/anti-D3 inflation survive moduli stabilization in warped string models containing Standard Model-like sectors, when the remaining light moduli evolve, and what tuning and CMB signatures result?

sources.title: From inflation to quintessence: a history of the universe in string theory

evidence.text: Can a moduli-stabilised type IIB effective theory accommodate high-scale inflation, reheating and late axion quintessence while retaining effective-field-theory control and satisfying cosmological constraints?

sources.title: String Cosmology

evidence.text: These lectures review how string theory might accommodate a small cosmological constant and inflation, emphasizing moduli stabilization, obstacles to flat inflaton potentials, possible remedies, and observational signatures.

sources.title: Finite temperature effects in modular cosmology

sources.title: Modulated Reheating and Large Non-Gaussianity in String Cosmology

evidence.text: Can an explicit string-inflation construction support a light field that modulates visible-sector reheating, dominates primordial curvature perturbations, and produces appreciable local non-Gaussianity while avoiding curvaton contributions?
